_meta.scope: Anderson (Madison County seat) and Lebanon (Boone County seat)
_meta.fair_housing: Places, rules, services and infrastructure only. No demographic, school, crime or 'family' content was collected. Lebanon's 'Welcome Home' new-resident page uses community/people-focused marketing language; only the service and provider facts were taken from it. Anderson's city Services page links a neighborhood crime-watch program, and Wikipedia's Anderson article includes population and institutional-affiliation material; none of that was used. Both codes contain fair-housing chapters (Anderson Ch. 95, Lebanon Ch. 93) that surfaced in 'rental' searches; they were not summarized. Search hits for 'Lebanon' short-term-rental special use permits came from Lebanon, ILLINOIS (lebanonil.org, 'Ordinance 1544') and were discarded.
_meta.note: Every URL in 'sources' was opened during this pass. Both municipal codes are on American Legal and were full-text searched with the site's own search API scoped to each code (terms: rental, landlord, tenant, 'rental registration', 'rental unit', 'rental property', 'short-term rental', 'short term rental', 'vacation rental', airbnb, tourist, transient, lodging, registration/registry, vacant, abandoned, 'bed and breakfast', deposit, inspection). Anderson's code is current through Ord. 11-26, passed 7-9-26, and includes the zoning ordinance as Chapter 160. Lebanon's code (the copy the city itself links as 'City Code') is the 2021 S-3 supplement, current only through Ord. 2020-15, passed 12-14-2020, so anything Lebanon adopted after December 2020 is not in it. Distances are straight-line, computed from city-center coordinates, matching the convention in owner-facts-west-south.json.
_meta.state_law: See owner-facts-west-south.json _meta for IC 36-1-20 (rental registration $5 cap, inspection limits, rental-use protection), IC 36-1-24 (short-term rentals) and the 2% residential property-tax cap (IC 6-1.1-20.6-7.5). Not re-researched.

anderson.jurisdiction: City of Anderson, the Madison County seat. Mostly Anderson Township, with small parts of Adams, Fall Creek, Lafayette, Richland and Union townships (township detail from Wikipedia only).
anderson.rental_rules: None found. The Anderson Code of Ordinances (current through Ord. 11-26, passed 7-9-26) has no rental registration, landlord registry, rental licensing or rental inspection chapter; scoped full-text searches for 'rental registration', 'rental unit', 'rental property' and 'registry' return nothing rental-related. Rules that do touch rentals: (1) Code 93.43: at the start of each lease the owner, manager or rental agent must install working smoke detectors (with an initial battery in battery units); the tenant maintains them during the tenancy, but hard-wired (AC) detectors stay the owner's responsibility. (2) Code Ch. 165 (Vacant and Abandoned Structures, adopting IC 36-7-36): an owner whose structure stays vacant 90+ consecutive days may face a $500 civil penalty, rising for each further 90-day period ($1,000, $1,500, then $2,000), capped at $5,000 per structure per year, unless the owner has filed approved documentation of intent with the enforcement authority (the Building Commissioner), is current on property taxes, and, among other options, the structure is maintained and actively offered for sale, lease or rent (165.99).
anderson.short_term_rentals: No Anderson-specific short-term rental rule found: 'short-term rental', 'vacation rental' and 'airbnb' appear nowhere in the code, including the zoning ordinance (Chapter 160), so state law (IC 36-1-24) is the governing framework. The zoning ordinance treats bed-and-breakfasts as a special exception use (160.46).
anderson.eviction_court: Madison County's caseload plan (LR48-AR00-02, as amended by Indiana Supreme Court order 25S-MS-211, effective January 1, 2026) assigns small claims (SC) and eviction (EV) filings 50/50 to Madison Circuit Court Division 4 and Division 5. Both sit on the 3rd floor of the Madison County Government Center, 16 E. 9th St., Anderson. Anderson City Court (1034 Main St.) lists its caseload as misdemeanors, infractions, city ordinance violations and 'limited civil matters'; it does not list evictions.
anderson.property_tax: Billed by the Madison County Treasurer (Government Center, 16 E. 9th St., Anderson); the treasurer's site gives 2026 due dates of May 11 and November 10. As a non-homestead single-family home, a rental is capped at 2% of gross assessed value under IC 6-1.1-20.6-7.5, before voter-approved referendum levies.

utilities.electric: Anderson Municipal Light & Power, the city's electric utility (outage line 765-648-6484; superintendent at 550 Dale Keith Jones Rd.). Billed by Anderson City Utilities (ACU) with water.
utilities.water: Anderson Water Department (city): two well fields with 16 wells and two treatment plants, about 10 million gallons a day, roughly 21,500 service connections. Started, stopped and transferred through the ACU Utility Office, 120 E. Eighth St. (765-648-6187).
utilities.sewer: City sewer (Water Pollution Control utility), billed by the city monthly based on metered water use. Code 51.23: sewer charges may be billed to the tenant, but that does not relieve the owner if the tenant doesn't pay; owners may examine the city's collection records.
utilities.stormwater: City stormwater fee (Code 51A.07). For a single-family rental it can be billed to the tenant only if written evidence is given to the utility office that the tenant agreed to pay; the charge remains the owner's ultimate responsibility. If a property has no water charges for 60+ days, the city opens a stormwater-only account payable by the owner.
utilities.gas: CenterPoint Energy, per the city's Utility Providers page.
utilities.trash: Best Way Disposal under the city contract (weekly trash, every-other-week recycling); the contract excludes commercial properties, including apartment complexes of three or more units.
utilities.account_rules: To open electric/water service a renter must provide a valid, unaltered copy of the lease listing all residents over 18, plus government photo ID; a new owner must show proof of ownership. Deposits are set by credit check and run $0 to $420 for residential service (Setting Up Service page; Code 52.04-52.05). An applicant must also pay in full any past-due ACU (electric, water, sewer) balance owed for the service premises, whether owed by the applicant or anyone else (52.04(B)(9)).

anderson.location: About 35 miles northeast of downtown Indianapolis (straight line). I-69 crosses the city's southeast corner, with access at exit 226 (SR 9/SR 109); SR 9 (Scatterfield Road) runs along the east side and SR 32 crosses the city center (highway detail from Wikipedia). The White River runs through the north part of the city. Mounds State Park (4306 Mounds Road) sits off I-69 just east of the city, with 10 prehistoric earthworks and six marked trails, including Trail 5 (2.5 miles) along the White River bluffs. The city also runs Anderson Regional Airport and Grandview Golf Course.
unverified: Anderson City Court civil jurisdiction: the court's page says 'limited civil matters' without detail. Whether it accepts any eviction filings (Indiana city courts can have limited civil jurisdiction) was not confirmed with the court or the Madison County Clerk. The page facts above rely on the county caseload plan, not on a statement that the city court cannot hear evictions.
Highway placement (I-69 exit 226, SR 9, SR 32) and the township list come from Wikipedia, not INDOT or the city.
Anderson Municipal Light & Power's service-area boundary: parts of the Anderson area may be served by Duke Energy or a REMC instead. Not mapped; the city page lists only Light & Power.
The Water Department's service area was reportedly expanded by an IURC order (news coverage); whether that changes which outlying addresses it serves was not checked.
Exact medium-risk deposit amount: Code 52.05 refers to the 52.30 fee schedule, which was not opened; only the $0-$420 range from the city's Setting Up Service page is used.
Trash billing: the city page doesn't say whether the Best Way Disposal charge appears on the ACU bill.
Whether the Ch. 165 vacant-structure penalty is actively enforced against residential rentals between tenants was not confirmed; the ordinance says an owner 'may be liable'.

lebanon.jurisdiction: City of Lebanon, the Boone County seat since 1832 (per the city's history page). The Boone County Courthouse, completed in 1911, stands on the original public square.
lebanon.rental_rules: None found, with a currency caveat. The Lebanon Code of Ordinances the city links (2021 S-3 supplement, current only through Ord. 2020-15, passed 12-14-2020) has no rental registration, licensing or inspection chapter; scoped searches for 'landlord', 'rental unit', 'rental property' and 'registration' return nothing rental-related. The city's code-enforcement landlord-tenant brochure describes complaint-driven enforcement: a written complaint goes to Planning & Zoning, and if violations are found the owner is contacted and given a deadline to correct them. Owner-relevant code rule: trash charges are billed to whoever is billed for water, and if a tenant is billed the owner is still liable for unpaid charges (51.058).
lebanon.short_term_rentals: No Lebanon-specific short-term rental rule found in the code or its Unified Development Ordinance (Title XV): 'short-term rental', 'vacation rental' and 'airbnb' do not appear. The UDO defines a bed-and-breakfast as an owner-occupied dwelling with up to five guest rooms for stays under two weeks, and lists it as a conditional use in the single-family (SF) district. State law (IC 36-1-24) is the governing framework. Because the online code stops at December 2020, a later STR ordinance would not show up here.
lebanon.eviction_court: All Boone County small claims, including evictions (EV), are filed in Boone Superior Court II, which has exclusive small claims jurisdiction under the county's local rules, at the Boone County Courthouse, 112 Courthouse Square, Lebanon. Re-checked this pass against both the local rules PDF and the court's page.
lebanon.property_tax: Billed by the Boone County Treasurer (209 Courthouse Square, Lebanon) in two installments due May 10 and November 10 under IC 6-1.1-22-9(a), the dates the treasurer's page quotes; statements are typically mailed in April. As a non-homestead single-family home, a rental is capped at 2% of gross assessed value under IC 6-1.1-20.6-7.5, before voter-approved referendum levies.

utilities.electric: Lebanon Utilities, a municipally owned utility (city-run electric since the 1930s; Service Board created 1942). Offices at 401 S. Meridian St. (765-482-5100); electric operations at 1300 W. Main St.
utilities.water: Lebanon Utilities (its own water department since 1894). Under the Citizens-Lebanon Water Supply Program begun in 2024, Citizens Energy Group has agreed to supply up to 25 million gallons a day to Lebanon Utilities as a wholesale customer.
utilities.sewer: Lebanon Utilities wastewater (sewage treatment since 1921); billed with electric and water.
utilities.gas: Not confirmed from an official source.
utilities.trash: WM (Waste Management), listed by the city as its residential trash and recycling provider; recycling enrollment and cancellation forms are handled through Lebanon Utilities.
utilities.account_rules: A renter opening an account must first have a Verification of Utility Customer form on file, signed by the owner or authorized representative, naming every adult who will live there, with photo ID for each; deposits are credit-based. By signing it, the owner gives up the ability to disconnect service while the tenant lives there (absent a court order) and is entitled to notice before a lien attaches for an unpaid sewer bill. To keep service on between tenants, the owner signs an Underlying Service Agreement: service rolls into the owner's name when a tenant's agreement ends, and the owner is billed for any usage without another agreement in place.

lebanon.location: About 25 miles northwest of downtown Indianapolis (straight line), 'just off I-65' per the city, with Lebanon exits at SR 39 (exit 139) and SR 32 (exit 140) and US 52 to the north (exit numbers from Wikipedia). The 3.3-mile Big Four Trail follows the former Big Four Railroad corridor through downtown; Memorial Park (40 acres, home of Seashore Waterpark) and Abner Longley Park (51 acres) are the largest city parks. The LEAP Lebanon Innovation District, launched by the IEDC, offers 9,000+ acres on the I-65 corridor and includes Lilly Lebanon API, which Lilly expects to be the largest active-pharmaceutical-ingredient production site in U.S. history; the State Road 32 realignment for the district is underway.
unverified: Code currency: Lebanon's online code stops at Ord. 2020-15 (12-14-2020). A rental registration, inspection or STR ordinance adopted since then would not appear. Confirm with the Clerk-Treasurer or Planning Department before publishing 'no registration requirement' as current.
Gas provider: third-party guides name CenterPoint Energy; no official city or utility page was found that says so.
Code 51.058 (owner liability for a tenant's trash charges) dates from 1979-80. Whether WM's charges are still billed on the Lebanon Utilities account under that rule was not confirmed.

Code 56.127 says stormwater for 'commercially owned residential property' is billed to the owner, not the tenant. Whether an individually owned single-family rental counts as 'commercially owned' was not clear, so it is left out of the summary.
New I-65 exit 143 (US 52 / LEAP Lebanon Boulevard) is reported by Wikipedia as opened October 2, 2026, replacing exit 141; no INDOT confirmation was found. Left out of the page text.
LEAP acreage: the IEDC page says '9,000+ available acres'; news reports of annexed acreage vary. Only the IEDC figure is used.
Utility deposit amounts: Lebanon Utilities says deposits are credit-based but publishes no amounts.
Exit numbers 139/140 come from Wikipedia, not INDOT.
